title: Russia Cosmetics Market 2026: Growth, Competition and Channels for Beauty Brands
excerpt: Russia's beauty market in 2026: Wildberries and Ozon sales, skincare, makeup, fragrance, retail trends and market-entry strategy for manufacturers.

blocks.text: Russia's online beauty market is expanding, but not every brand benefits equally

Russia's beauty market tells two different stories in 2026. Easy Commerce / Okkam estimates that beauty sales on major marketplaces reached RUB 504 billion in the first half of 2026, a 42% year-on-year increase. Reported growth was 70% on Ozon and 37% on Wildberries.

However, BusinesStat estimates total cosmetics sales in Russia declined by 2% in unit terms in 2025, to roughly 3.9 billion units. The measures cover different product baskets and periods. Rising marketplace sales should therefore not be mistaken for guaranteed demand for every new skincare or makeup SKU.
A manufacturer must understand which customer problem it solves, the achievable price and the reason a buyer would choose it over established Russian, Korean or international competitors.
What is growing: skincare, makeup, fragrance and men's grooming

Women's skincare remains a major market segment. Easy Commerce reported RUB 83 billion on Ozon in the first half of 2026, up 71%, and RUB 142 billion on Wildberries, up 23%. A new serum or moisturiser needs clear product positioning, credible claims and an appropriate price rather than a generic listing.

Makeup sales reached RUB 13 billion on Ozon (+74%) and RUB 56 billion on Wildberries (+39%). Shade accuracy, realistic photography and customer expectations are particularly important. For fragrance, the study reported almost RUB 50 billion on Wildberries (+72%) and RUB 5.4 billion on Ozon (+75%), highlighting the importance of authenticity, packaging and trust.

Men's grooming also deserves research: the report estimates RUB 14 billion on Ozon (+75%) and RUB 97 billion on Wildberries (+56%). These are category indicators, not guaranteed sales for a new shaving or hair-care item.
Methodology matters: the RUB 504 billion aggregate beauty figure includes some non-cosmetics items such as beauty devices and must not be presented as the market for creams alone.
Why the offline market is becoming more selective

Industry coverage in November 2026, citing N-Data Factory (formerly Nielsen), reported that the assortment of facial-care and colour-cosmetics brands in Russian offline chains fell 13.6% year on year in January–August 2026. Hair-care brand assortment declined 7.5%. These are assortment indicators, not equivalent revenue declines.

This means a manufacturer can face a growing digital channel and a more selective physical retailer simultaneously. A distributor may require evidence of product differentiation, credible positioning, sell-through and reliable supply rather than a catalogue alone.
A controlled marketplace launch followed by specialist retail can make sense for some brands, while professional or B2B channels may be a better initial route for others.
Wildberries, Ozon, specialist retailers and an owned website

Wildberries offers broad reach and significant beauty turnover, but platform visibility does not automatically produce profit. Ozon has shown rapid category growth, yet its audience, advertising economics and conversion should be measured separately.

Specialist retailers including Golden Apple and Letual may offer brand-positioning opportunities, subject to commercial negotiations and product eligibility. An owned Russian-language store can explain product routines and support permitted direct customer relationships, but needs Yandex SEO, advertising, VK content and CRM investment.

The ideal channel mix depends on price positioning, target buyer and repeat-purchase patterns. Our [Russia e-commerce guide](/en/blog/rusyada-e-ticaret-nasil-yapilir) explains the broader operational foundations.
What differentiates a Turkish beauty manufacturer, and what must be compliant?

Country of origin alone is not a sales argument. Formulation consistency, supported product benefits, packaging, price and reliable supply are stronger positioning factors. Starting with a focused product routine may be more manageable than a broad launch range. Avoid unsubstantiated medical or therapeutic claims.

Cosmetics are subject to applicable EAEU rules including TR CU 009/2011. Many items use a declaration of conformity; specified groups require state registration instead. A blanket statement that every cosmetic needs one generic EAC certificate is incorrect. Russian-language labelling, INCI, supported claims, relevant product classification and the phased Chestny ZNAK requirements should be checked SKU by SKU.
For detail see our [import guide](/en/blog/rusyaya-ithalat-sureci-turk-markalari-icin-adim-adim-rehber) and [marking guide](/en/blog/cestniy-znak-nedir-rusyada-hangi-urunlerde-zorunludur).
A controlled 90-day entry framework

Days 1–30: shortlist products, assess competition and price positioning, verify regulatory requirements and estimate viable unit economics. Days 31–60: prepare eligible product content, Russian descriptions, fulfilment and measured advertising tests. Days 61–90: review conversion, realised price, acquisition costs, reviews, returns and stock turnover; scale the promising SKUs and reconsider underperformers.

A single strong campaign does not prove long-term success. Repeat purchases, stock replenishment and contribution per order are more meaningful. For the full financial framework see our [marketplace unit economics guide](/en/blog/rusya-marketplace-unit-economics-karlilik-2026).
